title: warning_evaluate's `press` local retains the retired pressure word in core code
evidence:
press := make([dynamic]i64, int(state.bundles.n), int(state.bundles.n), context.temp_allocator)
defer delete(press)
...
press[bs] = fullest
...
new = congestion_level(press[bs] * 100 / lane_bound_units, w.pipe_amber_pct, w.pipe_red_pct)
detail: The sweep renamed the surrounding section comments ("Pipe congestion: per BUNDLE slot") and the level procs, but left the live `press` local — a retired-word identifier in core, inconsistent with the renamed pipe_congestion fields it feeds.
recommended_fix: Rename the local to `congest` (or `pipe_congestion`) in the three sites above.

title: Congestion_Level doc comment reads "Amber = congested/congested" (mechanical-rename artifact)
evidence:
// Congestion_Level — the tri-state warning level shared by nodes + pipes (4.1).
// None = healthy (no telegraph); Amber = congested/congested; Red = critical.
detail: The ruled rename collapsed the old "strained/pressured" pair into one word, leaving a tautological "congested/congested" that obscures the node-vs-pipe semantics in the enum's own doc.
recommended_fix: Rephrase, e.g. "Amber = congested (node or pipe); Red = critical".

title: Test failure message uses "congestion" as a verb: "must actually congestion a node"
evidence: testing.expectf(t, any_congested, "the fixture must actually congestion a node (non-vacuous pin)")
detail: Mechanical-rename grammar wart in a live test message (same pattern at node_health.odin:82 "never congestion" and warnings.odin:193). Message is what a future engineer reads when this pin fails.
recommended_fix: Rewrite as "the fixture must actually congest a node (non-vacuous pin)"; similarly fix node_health.odin:82 and warnings.odin:193.
